Wave 143, lane 143J. Live census read-only on 2026-10-23 (project hrvaqgvukzxfskkcrwbt). Proof: `npx tsx scripts/feature-certification-guard.ts` (package.json key to add: `"test:feature-certification": "tsx scripts/feature-certification-guard.ts"`).

## How to read a verdict

| Verdict | Means |
|---|---|
| CERTIFIED | Every link UI → action → domain → database is a real file / live table, at least one existing proof script names the row's files, the row needs no provider credential or owner decision, and no gap is open. It does **not** mean exercised live. |
| NOT CONFIGURED | Code complete and proven in-memory, but the advertised outcome needs a credential or owner decision this repository cannot supply. Presence in production is lane 143H's inventory, never assumed here. |
| PARTIAL | A link is missing or an advertised sub-capability is not delivered; the gap says which. |
| UNSUPPORTED | No implementation exists. |
| HIDDEN UNTIL AVAILABLE | Advertised in the plan catalogue but not deliverable — kept off every public surface until it is. |

**Nothing here has run for a customer.** The live database holds 2 brokerages, 2 subscriptions, 0 offers, 0 leads, 0 video projects, 0 podcast episodes, 0 email sends, 0 support tickets, 0 `agent_action_ledger` rows and 0 `platform_credentials` rows. Every chain below is proven by repository proofs and in-memory canaries (`npm run test:canaries`: 34 chains, 479 steps) — never by a live provider call.

## What the plans actually advertise (measured)

- `subscription_tiers.marketing_bullets` is **empty on all four tiers**: the public /pricing page renders no feature list from the database. Its promises are price, the trial, seat bands, seat packages, custom pricing and overage — row R29. No allowance number is hard-coded on any public surface (guarded).
- `subscription_tiers.features` carries 8 boolean flags; **no code reads any of them as a gate** — they describe the plan, they do not enforce it. Entitlement is the subscription state plus `feature_flags`.
- `feature_flags` holds 70 rows, all enabled at 100 % rollout; 2 are multi_location-only. 34 of the 70 keys are read by **no file** in app/ or lib/ — they are catalogue entries; the feature they name is gated by the paid-capability resolver (`mayUseAndAfford`), not by the key.
- `plan_limits` holds 17 metrics per tier; 12 are measured (counted by a writer or counted live), **5 are not**.

## Open owner decisions this audit surfaced

1. `feature_flags.custom_reports` is enabled for every tier but no report builder exists (R21). Disable it until one does — a data change, owner approval required, NOT applied here: `update feature_flags set enabled = false where feature_key = 'custom_reports';`
2. `plan_limits.ai_voice_minutes` and `subscription_tiers.features.limits.included_voice_minutes` are two spellings of one allowance; only the second is metered. Choose the allowance of record (§6).
3. The 5 unmeasured plan limits (ai_voice_minutes, emails_sent, live_assistant_minutes, sms_sent, storage_gb) have no writer. Until one lands they are not shown as usage and not named on plan cards; decide whether to build the writers or retire the rows.
4. The two multi_location-only flags are read by no gate (R23): the restriction is in the catalogue row only, and any tenant admin or broker can open the locations admin on any plan. Decide whether locations are a top-tier feature (then gate it with the paid-capability resolver) or a brokerage-tier one (then set the flags to match).
